rationale: Codebase-pin lens, all checks run against the bead worktree at 694b9d46 (clean, HEAD == reviewed commit). (1) AC-8(i): the three e2e variants in cmd/mindspec/next_claim_guard_test.go are REAL — nextReadyGateSetupSandbox requires real bd + real git on PATH (t.Fatalf when absent, no silent skip beyond the -short gate), builds the real mindspec binary, and each subtest constructs its own sandbox repo and claims only inside it. Each variant tests its NAMED dirt shape: untracked file (agent-notes.txt written, never added), untracked directory tree (scratch/ with two files; wantPath 'scratch/' matches porcelain's untracked-dir collapse), and a genuinely MODIFIED tracked file (AGENTS.md is written+committed by bootstrap.Run during sandbox setup, then overwritten). Each asserts claim success, absence of 'cannot claim work', the dirt path named in output, bead status in_progress, and the worktree created. Ran them: all three PASS (real bd, ~70s each). Vacuity check: 'AGENTS.md', 'agent-notes', and 'scratch/' appear nowhere in next's success-path output (grepped next.go, contextpack, instruct emitters), so the wantPath assertions genuinely pin the notice today. (2) AC-8(ii): TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_EnumerationPin is an honest real-claim git-status diff, not a mock — clean-before sanity gate, real 'mindspec next <bead>' run, porcelain-after parse excluding only .beads/issues.jsonl, exact length+membership match against next.EntangleableClaimPaths(). PASSES (119s, real bd). The empty-enumeration derivation's three facts verified in THIS repo: .mindspec/session.json is .gitignore line 3, .worktrees/ is gitignored, .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked (git ls-files) and is artifactPaths' sole entry. (3) next_dirty_test.go rewrite: the old file had exactly one test; the rewrite keeps the subprocess-real-binary shape, keeps the M6 double-emission pin ('Recovery steps:' / 'git restore .' banned in combined output), inverts the block assertion per R5.1, and adds a stderr-specific check that the notice names notes.txt (stderr captured separately, so this also pins the notice's stderr routing e2e). The only dropped coverage is the e2e assertion that the binary emits the Req 8/12 DirtyTreeFailure ('cannot claim work' + 'recovery:' + 'you are in the') — that trigger is now unreachable e2e by design (empty enumeration), and the full message contract is retained at unit level via assertDirtyTreeFailureInvariants inside the AC-8(iii) seam leg (recovery-line, no-destructive-advice, context-line-ordering invariants) plus the pre-existing DirtyTreeFailure unit tests. (4) release.go: UNTOUCHED by the commit (git diff name-only has no release files); it still calls next.CheckDirtyTree at cmd/mindspec/release.go:226, and CheckDirtyTree/CheckDirtyTreeDetail bodies are unchanged in guard.go — all-user-dirt-blocks semantics preserved; internal/complete's CheckDirtyTreeDetail use likewise unaffected. (5) Ran every new test file: internal/next entangle tests 10/10 PASS, internal/approve backfill tests 3/3 (5 legs) PASS, cmd/mindspec targeted e2e 3 variants + pin + dirty rewrite all PASS.

findings.title: Sandbox blanket .beads/ gitignore narrows the AC-8(ii) pin's sensitivity for .beads-resident writes
findings.detail: harness.NewSandbox replaces bootstrap's .gitignore with a hand-rolled list that ignores .beads/ WHOLESALE (internal/harness/sandbox.go:104), whereas real installs track .beads/issues.jsonl, .beads/config.yaml, etc. If a future claim step ever writes a tracked .beads path OTHER than the exempt issues.jsonl (e.g. mutating .beads/config.yaml), the pin test would stay green in the sandbox while real checkouts saw new dirt — the pin's 'red the moment a future claim step writes a tracked path this list omits' guarantee holds everywhere EXCEPT under .beads/. No such write exists today (verified: the claim path's bd interaction goes through bd itself, whose runtime files are the reason for the sandbox ignore). Non-blocking; worth a one-line comment on the pin test naming this blind spot, or a follow-up bead if .beads-resident claim writes ever appear.

findings.title: AC-8(i) notice assertions pin the path name, not the notice prefix
findings.detail: The e2e variants assert strings.Contains(out, wantPath) over CombinedOutput without also pinning the notice's distinctive prefix ('claiming despite unrelated dirty path'). Verified non-vacuous today (none of the three wantPath strings appear in next's success output), and the unit tests pin the notice function itself, so this is future-proofing only: a later feature that echoes file names into next's output could let the assertion pass without the notice. Adding the prefix to one variant's assertion would close it.

findings.title: cmd-level blocking branch is e2e-unreachable while the enumeration is empty (accepted by AC-8(iii)'s design)
findings.detail: next.go's 'if len(blockingDirt) > 0 { return next.DirtyTreeFailure(...) }' branch cannot be reached by any subprocess test today — SetEntangleableClaimPathsForTest is in-process only. The old next_dirty_test e2e pin of that emission is therefore gone, replaced by the unit-level seam leg (which does assert the full Req 8/12 message invariants via assertDirtyTreeFailureInvariants). This is inherent to R5.1's empty enumeration and matches AC-8(iii) as written ('seam leg ... refusal machinery stays live'); recording it so the gap is a documented decision, not an oversight. If the enumeration ever gains a real entry, the AC-8(ii) pin goes red first, and a cmd-level refusal e2e should be added in the same change.
